newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian government guarantees safety of prince.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian government guarantees safety of prince.

text.p: Cambodia's new government on Monday said it would guarantee the safety of ousted First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh if he returned to the country, but held firm to its position that the prince must face a court upon his return.

It also suggested it may be willing to hold talks with Ranariddh if he were found not guilty of charges Cambodian leader Hun Sen has levelled against him. The charges include weapons smuggling and bringing members of the Khmer Rouge guerilla group into the capital.

"I have talked with Hun Sen already and both of us will cooperate together to protect the safety of the prince when he returns, and he can bring the most intelligent lawyer in the world (with him)," said First Prime Minister Ung Huot, who was appointed to replace Ranariddh earlier this month.
"If the court finds the prince is not guilty, Hun Sen and I accept to hold political and other discussions with Prince Ranariddh," Ung Huot added in a statement he read on local radio.
Ung Huot invited members of the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) to send a delegation to Phnom Penh to review the evidence against Ranariddh.

Second Prime Minister Hun Sen overthrew Ranariddh , his former partner in Cambodia's coalition government, on July 6 after two days of fighting in the capital. Hun Sen has defended the power grab by accusing Ranariddh of bringing weapons and Khmer Rouge guerrillas into Phnom Penh.
